implementation.detail: Correction implementation commit 58c094f36b468c515d30ae1902a5057c7ff11b18 changes exactly three allowed files and no other file: tools/bpe_reference.py (SHA-256 7a58426db82bd49e6b3e992b55344e6e36e26410ae348cfb35169bc88322cabe), tools/test_bpe_reference.py (SHA-256 5607270e853718b80144ffdaf6c795e7fd78ee49b90fb1e8190218a8a88fe51b) and research/data/bpe-reference.md (SHA-256 1518f1e73414bd6ebd6335e579063bfc71be26b78d21e8707f53a4d3a0e0d181). validate_artifact now computes integer expansion lengths and rejects tokens above 4096 bytes before allocation; load_artifact caps serialized input at 64 KiB and requires canonical byte equality; encode caps raw UTF-8 input at 4096 bytes; token_ids_to_bytes/decode consume at most 4097 IDs and reject more than 4096 tokens or 4096 output bytes before extension. Adversarial doubling-chain, overlong JSON, generator and exact-boundary tests were added. Attempt-001 evidence is untouched.

unit_tests.detail: All acceptance commands exited 0 without timeout or retry: 30/30 corpus-reference tests (0.072546 s), 6/6 fixture tests (0.043723 s) and 28/28 BPE-reference tests (0.107550 s; 5 added) passed. The demo ran twice in 0.037137 s and 0.036300 s, producing byte-identical 4,343-byte output with SHA-256 bd743d70d6d0c96d9c6bc7780b8fe004e1a9520d3b47e7a43c3b10945543215e; artifact SHA-256 f67ef4ab5c343e3c9f81570b0d7426a5668e578aa84806058265d0aaf633ce7e and corpus digest 6fa4bbf3cc680d4058d067059545b787edf87eba3c87a71cd1013684ee99e8cd are unchanged from attempt-001. Demo training remains 6 documents/612 bytes, 1 quarantined document, 56 merges, actual vocabulary 320, all 8 held-out groups round-tripping and zero control IDs. The exact 4096 expansion/input/output boundaries are accepted; 8192 expansion, the 2^56 doubling chain, 64 KiB+ artifact, 4097-byte encode input, 4097-token generator and 4097-byte decoded output are rejected.

limitations: Synthetic documents only; no external corpus, source-rights decision, clearance, acquisition, PII filtering or benchmark corpus.
Small correctness oracle, not a production BPE trainer or an HF ByteLevel-equivalent tokenizer; it merges across whitespace and performs no regex pretokenization by design.
The 4096-byte expansion, encode-input and decoded-output caps are deliberate for this oracle; valid training documents cannot produce a longer token.
No cross-platform artifact equality claim until a separate Linux comparison verifies the canonical digest.
No quality, compression, fertility, throughput or downstream model claim.
No production tokenizer backend, special-token training, sentencepiece/HF compatibility, sharding, streaming or serving work.
Document text has strict UTF-8/surrogate rejection and IDs are nonempty and unique; separate metadata-surrogate hardening is not claimed.
